description:
pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs:314-385 implements both from_pem and from_der_iter
as 'fail-fast': the first malformed cert stops processing and the function
returns Err, dropping any anchors successfully decoded so far.

This is a defensible default but it is the only behavior offered. A caller
who needs to recover usable anchors from a partially-corrupt bundle (a
real production scenario — see below) has no API path.

Real-world scenarios where partial-load matters:

  - A distro CA bundle ships with one cert that has malformed DER in a
    rarely-exercised extension (e.g., a malformed CertificatePolicies). The
    cert is otherwise valid and the rest of the bundle is fine. The
    deployment wants to load 146 anchors and warn about #84, not crash on
    boot.
  - A custom enterprise bundle is built by automation. One CA is in the
    process of being rotated; the new cert is malformed because the
    automation has a bug. The deployment wants to continue serving with
    the old anchors while the team fixes the new one.
  - A CT-log-scraping ingester pulls 100k roots from a public source. A
    handful are corrupt. The ingester wants to load all good ones and log
    the bad ones for follow-up.

What goes wrong for callers in production today:

  - Caller has two options: (i) call from_pem on the whole bundle and
    accept all-or-nothing, or (ii) parse PEM themselves, call from_der
    per block, accumulate errors, and call from_der_iter ... but wait,
    from_der_iter is also fail-fast. So they need to call from_der
    individually. That means the 'canonical adapter entry point'
    (lib.rs:356) is unusable for the partial-load case.
  - Callers will write their own PEM splitter, defeating the 'one place
    for parsing' design goal (lib.rs:359-360).
  - The fail-fast default propagates to adapter crates
    (pkix-truststore-system, pkix-truststore-pkcs11): if those adapters
    accumulate DER bytes and feed them to from_der_iter, one bad cert
    from a partially-corrupt OS trust store crashes the whole load.
    Less acceptable in HSM/KMS contexts where individual key handles can
    fail transiently.

Fix options:

  a) Document the fail-fast contract explicitly (the function-level doc on
     from_pem already says 'Returns Error::Pem or Error::Der on the first
     malformed block' — extend the same to from_der_iter).
  b) Add a variant that collects all errors:
       pub fn from_pem_partial(bytes: &[u8])
         -> (Vec<TrustAnchor>, Vec<(usize, Error)>);
     Returns both successful anchors and per-index errors.
  c) Add a callback-based variant:
       pub fn from_pem_with_handler<F>(bytes: &[u8], handler: F)
         -> Result<Vec<TrustAnchor>, Error>
       where F: FnMut(usize, &Error) -> ControlFlow<(), ()>;
     Caller decides on each error whether to continue or stop.

Option (a) is the cheap fix for the doc contract. (b) and (c) close the
behavioral gap. Pre-1.0 is the right window to pick.

Flagged 'opinion' because reasonable libraries (e.g., rustls-webpki) do
fail-fast and require callers to roll their own splitter; this is a real
ergonomics question but not a security issue.
title: No partial-load API: one bad cert in a 147-cert bundle fails the entire load
